description.value: Lowhee Campground puts 80 well-treed sites in a quiet forest-to-wetland setting at Barkerville Historic Town & Park, Canada's largest living history museum and a National Historic Site; flush toilets, coin showers, and a playground are on-site, but access is seasonal (mid-June to late September only).

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Lowhee Campground is an active 80-site campground within Barkerville Historic Town & Park, open June 18–September 28 2026, with potable water in three washroom buildings, a coin-operated shower house, bear-proof bins, and 47 advance-reservable sites; OSM tags (drinking_water=yes, shower=yes, reservation=yes, tents=yes) align well with this. The visitor information page explicitly notes cycling rules for the Barkerville site, which is relevant context for touring cyclists. The website content was truncated before full Lowhee site-type details (e.g. whether power hookups are available at Lowhee specifically) could be confirmed.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, well-facilitated campground within a major BC heritage park and National Historic Site; provides touring cyclists with water, showers, bear-proof storage, and reservable sites along a remote Interior cycling corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: Cycling is not permitted within the Barkerville historic townsite; cyclists must check in at the Welcome Centre and walk bikes through the Heritage Zone during main season.
